emergence-emergence:ashbyhq:3daa8d91-dc6.title: Director
emergence-emergence:ashbyhq:3daa8d91-dc6.description: Director, Emergence | New York - Full-Time / Part-Time | Onsite Our Platform We’re a thematic holding company backed by the Pritzker Organization focused exclusively on acquiring and scaling category-defining businesses. Our structure organizes investments into focused portfolios that function as specialized operating groups, each developing deep domain expertise, proven operational playbooks and long-term partnerships with founders and management teams. We combine operational rigor with permanent capital backing and a growth equity mindset - partnering closely with leadership teams to drive sustainable ARR growth, profitability improvements and industry-leading customer outcomes. The Role We’re hiring roles from the Associate to VP level to be a core part of our sourcing and origination function. You will partner with firm leadership to help lead pre-LOI activities, from identifying, diligence, dealmaking, closing, and overall owning this stage of the investment lifecycle. You will be required to utilize your own investment judgment to decide what companies we should pursue and where we should spend our time. You will be the first layer of investment judgment in our entire organization. This is a foundational hire - you will work directly with the team to build out this function and lead and drive forward investments from end to end, with real ownership over how we build this team and process from the ground up. You will help build repeatability and scalability into our sourcing process. This includes thinking across processes, people, and technology. Key Responsibilities - Source and evaluate software acquisition opportunities using your own investment judgment. - Maintain and improve sourcing infrastructure: outbound systems, coverage models, intermediary relationships. - Drive due diligence processes and coordinate cross-functional workstreams with advisors and stakeholders. - Support deal structuring, negotiation, transaction execution, and overall dealmaking. - Collaborate with portfolio company leadership on post-acquisition strategy and add-on acquisitions. - Help hire and develop team members as Emergence grows. Ideal Qualifications - 4-10+ years of private equity / growth equity / VC investing experience preferred. All experience levels are open to apply - Growth and sales roles at fast growing startups are also accepted - Strong investment judgment, deep understanding of enterprise software, and exceptional communication skills with founders and management teams - Ability to run through walls and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment - Genuine interest in helping grow and operate exceptional software companies - A builder mentality - you’re energized by the opportunity to help shape something early and not just execute within an established playbook Compensation - Cash compensation very competitive, exceeds roles at other firms by high margin. - Uncapped cash bonus potential. - Ability to participate in long-term carry programs aligned with seniority and performance. - Meaningful upside for the right person — compensation structure designed to scale with you as firm and team grow. If you're interested in investing in and scaling high-quality software businesses alongside a small, entrepreneurial team backed by permanent capital, we'd love to connect!

jobgether-jobgether:lever:5d27a30b-860c-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Resource Operations Analyst Assistant based in the United States. This role supports a mission-critical Department of Defense program focused on strengthening financial auditability and global transportation logistics. You will work at the intersection of workforce planning, program operations, recruiting, compliance, and resource management. The position partners closely with program leadership to ensure teams are appropriately staffed, onboarded, supported, and aligned with operational priorities. You’ll use workforce data and reporting to identify trends, gaps, risks, and opportunities for improvement. The role also involves coordinating sensitive onboarding and clearance processes in a highly regulated environment. With opportunities to exercise judgment and ownership, you’ll contribute directly to the readiness and effectiveness of a high-visibility program. Analyze staffing trends, workforce gaps, and resource data to support informed planning decisions and identify operational risks or optimization opportunities. Maintain and improve workforce tracking tools, dashboards, reports, and metrics, ensuring data accuracy and integrity. Coordinate end-to-end onboarding activities, ensuring personnel, systems, tools, documentation, and access are ready before employees begin. Identify and resolve onboarding delays or risks, continuously improving processes for efficiency, scalability, and compliance. Evaluate candidate submissions against program requirements, skills, labor categories, and workforce needs, providing recommendations to recruiting and hiring stakeholders. Coordinate interviews and help deliver a professional, efficient candidate experience. Review employment and onboarding documentation for completeness and accuracy while ensuring compliance with federal, DoD, and program-specific requirements. Monitor security clearance status and onboarding compliance, escalating risks and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies. Serve as a liaison between internal teams, subcontractors, and external partners to coordinate workforce operations, onboarding, and access. Analyze workforce information to identify trends and provide leadership with actionable insights and recommendations. Oversee employee offboarding and lifecycle activities, ensuring compliance, continuity, risk mitigation, and accurate documentation. Identify opportunities to improve workforce processes, reporting, onboarding, and offboarding practices across the program. Requirements: Bachelor’s degree required. Active Secret security clearance required. Strong organizational and analytical skills, with the ability to manage multiple workforce and operational priorities simultaneously. Ability to analyze staffing information, workforce trends, and operational data and translate findings into useful recommendations. Strong attention to detail when handling employment documentation, clearance information, workforce records, and compliance requirements. Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when working with sensitive personnel and program information. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with program leadership, hiring managers, recruiters, subcontractors, and external partners. pearvc-pear-vc:ashbyhq:4f94427f-f267-402.title: Accounts Receivable Specialist - NeuroNav
pearvc-pear-vc:ashbyhq:4f94427f-f267-402.description: [https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/cca476c0-947e-4006-a2cb-409350de667a/57653a9c-9443-4a76-bdae-82ea973e9a67/Job%20Posting%20Logo%201%20(600%20x%20200%20px)%20(600%20x%20175%20px).png] Remote - Part Time - 20 Hours per week Do you thrive on keeping financial operations running precisely — and want your work to directly fund services for adults with developmental disabilities? We're looking for an experienced Accounts Receivable Specialist with strong bookkeeping and QuickBooks skills who is ready to be the financial backbone of one of California's fastest-growing disability care organizations. At NeuroNav, we believe people with disabilities deserve autonomy, real power over their services, and the support of a team that genuinely cares. Our mission is to enhance the quality of life for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities through simplicity and choice. We specialize in helping families navigate California's Self-Determination Program (SDP) — a state-funded Medicaid program that offers more creative and flexible choice in how disability dollars are spent. This is a mission-critical role. When our finances run smoothly, families get faster access to life-changing services. You'll work closely with our CEO and bookkeeper to ensure NeuroNav stays in strong financial health — and as NeuroNav grows, there is strong potential for this part-time role to expand into a full-time finance and operations position. About NeuroNav Founded at Stanford in 2020 with support from the Stanford Innovation Fellowship, NeuroNav is California's largest independent Self-Determination Program facilitator. As a public benefit corporation, we combine technology with a compassionate team of expert Navigators to help adults with IDD — including those with autism and cerebral palsy — access and manage self-directed Medicaid services. We've helped hundreds of families enroll in the Self-Determination Program and are scaling rapidly, backed by Pear VC, the same investors behind DoorDash, Gusto, and Heap. Responsibilities include: - Accounts Receivable & Invoicing — own end-to-end accounts receivable, including sending invoices to payors (nonprofits and government agencies), obtaining missing authorizations and following up on outstanding payments. - Account Reconciliation — perform regular reconciliation across all accounts to ensure financial records are accurate and audit-ready. - Bookkeeping & QuickBooks Management — maintain clean, organized records in QuickBooks Online and support accounts payable and expense management with assistance from our bookkeeper. - Financial Tracking & Reporting — assist with budgeting, financial tracking, and management reporting to support leadership decision-making. - Process Improvement — streamline core financial and operations processes and tools to support a scaling organization. - Office & HR Operations Support — support remote office management, asset management, basic legal tasks (e.g., business insurance, mail), and HR processes in partnership with our PEO providers. What You'll Bring - 3+ years of accounting, operations, or finance experience (5+ years preferred) - 2+ years of bookkeeping experience (required) - 2+ years of hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online (required) - Demonstrated experience with invoicing and account reconciliation (required) - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or equivalent practical experience - Strong proficiency in Excel - Experience working in a CPA firm (preferred) - Experience with medical billing or healthcare finance (preferred) - 1+ years of finance/operations experience at a Series B or earlier-stage startup (preferred) - Experience in a customer-facing role (preferred) - Experience with general HR administration or PEO providers (preferred) - Experience with strategic finance — forecasting, GAAP accounting, budgeting, or corporate planning (preferred) Benefits We believe in supporting our employees'
